Header: Hypothenemus hampei (Ferrari) Sinhala - Badari gulla, Tamil- Copi pala thullaipan

Prevention: Limit the harvesting to three times and remove and destroy all the leftover berries from tree and the ground
Cultivate varieties showing uniform maturity e.g:
Conserve the natural enemies by keeping high plant diversity, in particular plants providing nectar
Monitoring: Watch out for small holes in the disc region of berries and black colour seeds inside the berry
Collect random sample of berries and count infested/ un- infested ones
Consider action when more than 4% berries are infested
Direct Control: Use traps with methanol and ethanol (1:1) as a lure for collecting the female insects.
Separate the damaged berries at harvest and deep burry (1 m) or destroy by burning
After seed separation, dip seeds in hot water for 2 – 3 minutes.
Restrictions: Preventive measures are more effective against this pest than chemical control.
Any pesticide application has to be done before the adult beetles lay eggs.
The best time to spray is when the adult females are flying around looking for new homes.
This happens all year long but happens most often at 60 days and 150 days after flowering.
This is usually at the growth stage of older not yet hardened berries close to maturity.
However, there are currently no least or slightly toxic products available
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
